chunks.heading: Safety Controls
chunks.text: stored under the cleanup root.. Pre-delete recheck: Purpose Re-discovers active table locations and write paths immediately before deletion, and stops if a table's storage can no longer be resolved.. exclude_paths: Purpose Protects explicitly configured storage paths.. exclude_database_folders: Purpose Protects database-relative folders without requiring full object-storage paths.. Sentinel folder exclusion: Purpose Skips Spark/Hadoop staging folders such as _temporary and .spark-staging.. older_than_hours: Purpose Skips folders with recently written objects, and folders whose age cannot be established.. max_candidate_folders_per_database: Purpose Skips cleanup when too many candidates are detected.. Empty-database guard: Purpose Skips databases with no active table locations.. Catalog-scoped storage access: Purpose Uses the selected catalog's own storage settings, and fails closed if they cannot be resolved.. Unresolved ownership guard: Purpose Blocks deletion for a database when any table's storage location cannot be established.. Audit integrity guard: Purpose Stops deleting for the rest of the run if an audit row cannot be written.. Audit table: Purpose Records the outcome for each database..

chunks.title: Cleanup Untracked Table Folders Job
chunks.heading: Object Storage Access
chunks.text: You do not configure storage settings or credentials for this job. Cleanup always uses the storage configuration associated with the catalog you selected in `catalog`. If that storage configuration cannot be resolved safely, the job stops for that database and records `FAILED`. It does not fall back to any other storage configuration. This helps ensure cleanup remains within the storage associated with the selected catalog. The job cleans databases stored on S3-compatible storage, Google Cloud Storage, or Azure storage. A database stored on another filesystem, such as HDFS, is skipped with `status_reason=invalid_storage_location`.

chunks.title: Cleanup Untracked Table Folders Job
chunks.heading: Storage Roots
chunks.text: The job deletes folders only under one location per database, the **cleanup root**. It chooses the cleanup root from the database's table locations: when the tables share one parent folder, that folder is the cleanup root; otherwise the job uses the database location. The cleanup root must stay inside the database location, or the same path without the `.db` suffix. When tables are stored under more than one parent folder, table locations outside the cleanup root are not checked in that run. The job reports them under `TABLE LOCATIONS OUTSIDE THE SCANNED ROOT`, and a successful audit row gets `status_reason=partial_scan_coverage`. The job also lists other roots one level deep for review. **Nothing in these report-only roots is ever deleted.** A root is listed when it sits inside the database's own storage: - the database location, or the same path without the `.db` suffix; - for `spark_catalog` and IOMETE-managed REST catalogs, the catalog's namespace folder for the database; - a location you approve in `report_only_storage_roots`, as long as at least one visible table of the database is stored under it. { "report_only_storage_roots": } Report-only roots are never deleted. A folder in a report-only root that is not matched to a visible

chunks.title: Cleanup Untracked Table Folders Job
chunks.heading: Storage Roots
chunks.text: visible table of the database is stored under it. { "report_only_storage_roots": } Report-only roots are never deleted. A folder in a report-only root that is not matched to a visible table is not necessarily orphaned, because a table the job cannot see may own it. Approved report-only roots are not fully checked for ownership across databases. Each key must be listed in `databases`. Approve only locations that belong to the database they are listed under. The job does not compare approved locations with the storage of other databases. Other table parents are reported as `not_scanned` with a reason: outside_database_boundary: Meaning The parent is outside the database's own storage, in the same or another bucket.. bucket_root: Meaning The parent is a bucket root.. contains_warehouse_root: Meaning The parent equals or contains the catalog warehouse root.. inside_table_location: Meaning The parent sits inside another table's folder.. contains_database_storage: Meaning The location would contain the database's own location or namespace folder.. no_visible_table: Meaning An approved location holds no visible table of the database.. invalid_location: Meaning The location cannot be parsed.. root_limit_reached: Meaning More than 25 additional roots were found; the rest are not listed.. Folders in report-only roots that do not belong to a visible table

chunks.title: Cleanup Untracked Table Folders Job
chunks.heading: Storage Roots
chunks.text: location cannot be parsed.. root_limit_reached: Meaning More than 25 additional roots were found; the rest are not listed.. Folders in report-only roots that do not belong to a visible table are listed under `FOLDERS IN REPORT-ONLY ROOTS NOT MATCHED TO A VISIBLE TABLE`. A table the job cannot see may still own them, so treat them as items to review, not as orphans.

chunks.title: Cleanup Untracked Table Folders Job
chunks.heading: Excluding Paths
chunks.text: Use `exclude_paths` when you know the full object-storage path to protect. Each entry must include a scheme and bucket: Use `exclude_database_folders` when you want to protect a folder relative to a configured database: A folder is skipped when it equals an excluded path, contains one, or sits inside one. Paths are compared by whole path segments, so `manual_archive` does not protect `manual_archive_v2`. A `database.folder` exclusion also applies to the same folder name under every report-only root of that database. Both forms are included in the effective excluded-path list written to the audit table.

chunks.title: Cleanup Untracked Table Folders Job
chunks.heading: Other Databases and Iceberg Write Paths
chunks.text: Before choosing candidates, the job reads the location of every database it can see in the catalog. Storage of another database at or inside the cleanup root is protected and is never a candidate. On catalogs with many databases this step can take some time; the driver log reports how many databases were read and how long it took. If the storage of other databases cannot be established, for example because a database location cannot be read, the database is `BLOCKED` with `status_reason=other_database_storage_unknown` and nothing is deleted. For Iceberg tables, folders named by `write.data.path`, `write.metadata.path`, `write.object-storage.path`, and `write.folder-storage.path` are protected like the table location, both during candidate detection and in the pre-delete recheck.

chunks.title: Cleanup Untracked Table Folders Job
chunks.heading: Audit Table
chunks.text: The job writes audit rows to: spark_catalog.iomete_system_db.cleanup_untracked_table_folder_runs Use the audit table to review candidates, skipped databases, deleted folders, runtime metadata, and failure details.

For databases skipped with `database_location_is_bucket_root`, `database_location_contains_warehouse_root`, or `scan_root_outside_database_boundary`, the job still lists report-only roots whose own checks pass and prints a `STORAGE ROOT REPORT` in the driver logs. Nothing is deleted.

chunks.title: Cleanup Untracked Table Folders Job
chunks.heading: Partial Deletion and Audit Failures
chunks.text: Candidate folders are deleted one at a time. If a folder cannot be deleted, the job stops for that database and records `FAILED` with `status_reason=deletion_failed`. - `deleted_folder_count` and `deleted_folders` list only the folders confirmed deleted before the failure, so they can be greater than zero on a `FAILED` row. - `diagnostic_details.deletion_failed_folder_path` names the folder that failed. Check it in object storage before the next run. - Other configured databases continue, as long as this database's audit row was written. If an audit row cannot be written during a run, the job no longer has a reliable record of what it did. It deletes no more folders in that run, records later databases that would have been eligible for deletion as `BLOCKED` with `status_reason=audit_integrity_lost`, and fails at the end of the run. A database whose own audit row failed has no row in the audit table; use the driver log for that database.

chunks.title: Cleanup Untracked Table Folders Job
chunks.heading: Unresolved Table Storage Ownership
chunks.text: A table is unresolved when it exists in the catalog but the job cannot establish which storage it owns. This includes a table whose Iceberg metadata, location, or properties cannot be read, a table with a missing or blank location (views excepted), a location without a scheme and bucket, an Iceberg table with `gc.enabled` set to anything but `true` or with `write.location-provider.impl` set, and an Iceberg write path that is blank or has no scheme and bucket. This does not mean the table is unhealthy or unwanted. It only means the job does not know which storage folder that table owns. Storage reconciliation still runs and reports what it found. What changes is what the job is allowed to conclude. If any table in the database is unresolved, that table could own any of the unmatched folders, so no folder in that database can be proven untracked. For that database: - Every unmatched folder is reported as potentially untracked, not as a candidate. - `potentially_untracked_folder_count` carries those folders, and `candidate_folder_count` stays `0`. - Nothing is deleted, in dry-run mode or in deletion mode. - The audit row is written with `status=BLOCKED` and `status_reason=unresolved_catalog_ownership`. Other configured databases are unaffected and continue

chunks.title: Cleanup Untracked Table Folders Job
chunks.heading: Unresolved Table Storage Ownership
chunks.text: stays `0`. - Nothing is deleted, in dry-run mode or in deletion mode. - The audit row is written with `status=BLOCKED` and `status_reason=unresolved_catalog_ownership`. Other configured databases are unaffected and continue to run.

chunks.title: Cleanup Untracked Table Folders Job
chunks.heading: Understanding Summary Logs
chunks.text: At the end of each database, the job prints a `CLEANUP REPORT` block in the driver logs. The header shows the run mode: `Mode: dry run, nothing is deleted` or `Mode: deletion enabled`. Its sections are: CATALOG: Source Catalog metadata, Meaning Counts of tables found, tables with verified storage locations, and tables whose storage location could not be read.. TABLES WHOSE STORAGE LOCATION COULD NOT BE RESOLVED: Source Catalog metadata, Meaning Tables that exist in the catalog but whose storage could not be established. Shown only when there are any.. STORAGE: Source Object-storage scan, Meaning Counts of folders discovered under the cleanup root, folders belonging to verified catalog tables, folders protected or skipped for other reasons, and folders with no verified owner.. STORAGE FOLDERS PROTECTED BY A VERIFIED CATALOG TABLE: Source Catalog metadata, Meaning Active table locations discovered from the catalog. These are the protection set and must not be deleted. This list may include paths outside the cleanup root.. STORAGE FOLDERS EXCLUDED BY CONFIGURATION: Source Configuration, Meaning Paths protected by exclude_paths or exclude_database_folders.. STORAGE FOLDERS PROTECTED OR SKIPPED FOR OTHER REASONS: Source Candidate detection, Meaning Folders that are excluded, belong to another database or an Iceberg write path, are

chunks.title: Cleanup Untracked Table Folders Job
chunks.heading: Understanding Summary Logs
chunks.text: by exclude_paths or exclude_database_folders.. STORAGE FOLDERS PROTECTED OR SKIPPED FOR OTHER REASONS: Source Candidate detection, Meaning Folders that are excluded, belong to another database or an Iceberg write path, are framework working folders, or are too new or of unknown age. Shown only when there are any.. TABLE LOCATIONS OUTSIDE THE SCANNED ROOT: Source Catalog metadata, Meaning Table locations outside the cleanup root. Storage around them was not checked in this run.. STORAGE ROOTS: Source Object-storage scan, Meaning The cleanup root and report-only roots, with their status (scanned, absent, or listing_failed) and the roots that were not scanned.. FOLDERS IN REPORT-ONLY ROOTS NOT MATCHED TO A VISIBLE TABLE: Source Object-storage scan, Meaning Folders in report-only roots that no visible table owns. These are never deleted.. TABLE LOCATIONS OUTSIDE EVERY LISTED ROOT: Source Catalog metadata, Meaning Table locations that no listed root covers.. UNTRACKED STORAGE FOLDERS: Source Candidate detection, Meaning Folders that were not protected and passed the cleanup filters. These are the folders the job would delete in deletion mode. When deletion is blocked, this section is titled UNTRACKED STORAGE FOLDERS (DELETION BLOCKED).. POTENTIALLY UNTRACKED STORAGE FOLDERS: Source Candidate detection, Meaning Shown instead of the section above when a table's

chunks.title: Cleanup Untracked Table Folders Job
chunks.heading: Understanding Summary Logs
chunks.text: When deletion is blocked, this section is titled UNTRACKED STORAGE FOLDERS (DELETION BLOCKED).. POTENTIALLY UNTRACKED STORAGE FOLDERS: Source Candidate detection, Meaning Shown instead of the section above when a table's storage location could not be established. These folders have no verified catalog owner, but they cannot be proven untracked, so none of them are deletion candidates.. DELETION: Source Deletion result, Meaning Folders actually deleted when dry_run=false and delete_enabled=true, Dry run. No folder was deleted. in dry-run mode, or BLOCKED with the reason when deletion was prevented.. In short, catalog active table locations come from catalog metadata, while storage folders come from the physical object-storage scan.

chunks.title: Cleanup Untracked Table Folders Job
chunks.heading: Known Limitations
chunks.text: - Ownership is checked against the tables and databases the job can see in the catalog. A table or database the job cannot see does not protect its folder. - Another database's table stored at a custom location inside the cleanup root is not protected. - Files that an Iceberg table reaches without a write path property, for example through `add_files`, `migrate`, `snapshot`, or an earlier table location, are not protected. - A Hive partition stored outside its table's folder is not protected. - The job deletes whole untracked table folders, not individual orphan files inside active table folders. - Folder names are compared case-sensitively, because `ORDERS` and `orders` are different object-storage prefixes. - A database whose location equals or contains the catalog warehouse root cannot be cleaned by this job. - Catalogs that use vended or remotely signed credentials are not supported for storage access. - Folder age and size require listing every object in each candidate folder. This can take time for folders with many objects.

chunks.title: Cleanup Untracked Table Folders Job
chunks.heading: Summary
chunks.text: Use this job to review and optionally clean table folders that remain in object storage after tables are no longer tracked by the catalog. Always start with dry-run mode, review the audit table, and enable deletion only after confirming that the candidates are safe to remove.

chunks.title: Data Compaction Job
chunks.text: --- Iceberg tables slow down over time as small files, old snapshots, and unused files pile up. The **Data Compaction Job** cleans them up on a schedule. For every Iceberg table it processes, it runs four maintenance operations: - **Rewrite manifests**: reorganizes table metadata for faster planning. See Rewrite Manifests. - **Rewrite data files**: merges small files into larger ones. See Compact Data Files. - **Expire snapshots**: removes old snapshots. See Expire Snapshots. - **Remove orphan files**: deletes files no snapshot refers to. See Delete Orphan Files. Tables in other formats, such as Hive or Parquet tables, are skipped. IOMETE also offers built-in Table Maintenance (beta), which runs these operations automatically when a table needs them. Use either the built-in feature or this job for a given table, not both. - **Version:** `1.2.14` (see the Marketplace Jobs release notes for the latest version) - **Source:** View on GitHub

chunks.title: Data Compaction Job
chunks.heading: Marketplace
chunks.text: Open **Job Templates** and click **Marketplace**. Find the **data-compaction** card, click the **⋮** menu, and select **Deploy**. The job form opens pre-filled with recommended defaults and a weekly schedule. Review the config file (see Configuration), then click **Create**.

chunks.title: Data Compaction Job
chunks.heading: Manual Setup
chunks.text: Open **Job Templates** in the sidebar and click . **1. Name, Schedule, and Application** - **Name:** any name you like, for example `data-compaction` - **Schedule:** select **Cron** and enter `0 12 * * 0` (every Sunday at 12:00). Use any cron expression that fits your needs. Without a schedule, the job only runs when you start it. - **Application type:** `Python` - **Docker registry:** `default` - **Docker image:** `iomete/iomete_data_compaction:1.2.14` (replace with the latest version) - **Main application file:** `local:///app/driver.py` **2. Config File** Under **Configurations**, select the **Config Maps** tab and click **Add config**. Set **File path** to `/etc/configs/application.conf` and paste the HOCON template below. { catalog: "spark_catalog", expire_snapshot: , rewrite_data_files: { options: { "min-input-files": 2, "target-file-size-bytes": 536870912 } } } **3. Instance Resources** Pick driver and executor instance types that fit the size of your tables. Click to save the job.

chunks.title: Data Compaction Job
chunks.heading: Configuration
chunks.text: The config file is HOCON. Only `catalog` is required. Every other field is optional and falls back to the default shown below.

chunks.title: Data Compaction Job
chunks.heading: Choosing Tables
chunks.text: By default the job processes every table in every database of the catalog. catalog: Default required, Description The catalog to compact, for example spark_catalog.. databases: Default [], Description Databases to process. Empty means all databases in the catalog.. table_include: Default [], Description Tables to process. See the notes below.. table_exclude: Default [], Description Tables to skip.. Tables in `table_include` and `table_exclude` can be written as `database.table` to target one table, or as `table` to match that name in every database. Write table names in lowercase and without quotes, here and in `table_overrides`. A name that doesn't match a table is skipped without a warning. - `table_include` only limits the databases it mentions. Databases with no table in the list are still processed in full. To compact only a few tables, also set `databases` to just the databases those tables are in. - If `table_include` is in the config at all, even as `[]`, `table_exclude` is ignored. Leave `table_include` out when you use `table_exclude`.

chunks.title: Data Compaction Job
chunks.heading: Operation Settings
chunks.text: Each operation has its own block. Set `enabled: false` in a block to skip that operation. With the default settings, each run keeps only the latest snapshot of every table. You cannot time travel to earlier versions, and long-running queries can fail. Set `expire_snapshot.older_than_days` or a higher `retain_last` if you need history. A snapshot is kept if it is one of the last `retain_last` snapshots, or if it is newer than `older_than_days`. expire_snapshot.enabled: Default true, Description Run snapshot expiration.. expire_snapshot.retain_last: Default 1, Description Always keep the N most recent snapshots.. expire_snapshot.older_than_days: Default not set, Description Remove snapshots older than N days. When not set, any snapshot older than 5 minutes can be removed.. remove_orphan_files.enabled: Default true, Description Run orphan file cleanup.. remove_orphan_files.older_than_days: Default 1, Description Only delete orphan files older than N days. Set this longer than your longest-running write, or files from a write still in progress can be deleted.. rewrite_data_files.enabled: Default true, Description Run data file compaction.. rewrite_data_files.strategy: Default binpack, Description binpack merges small files. sort also sorts rows, which is slower but can speed up queries.. rewrite_data_files.sort_order: Default not set, Description Columns to sort by when strategy is sort, for example "user_id ASC, event_time DESC".. rewrite_data_files.where: Default

chunks.heading: Operation Settings
chunks.text: rows, which is slower but can speed up queries.. rewrite_data_files.sort_order: Default not set, Description Columns to sort by when strategy is sort, for example "user_id ASC, event_time DESC".. rewrite_data_files.where: Default not set, Description Only compact rows that match this SQL filter, for example "date . To change the schedule, edit the job and set the **Schedule** parameter (cron expression).

chunks.title: File Streaming Job
chunks.text: --- The **File Streaming Job** continuously ingests files from object storage into an Iceberg table using Spark Structured Streaming. Point it at a source directory, or an SQS queue that notifies on new files, and it appends new files to the destination table on a fixed trigger interval. - **Version:** `1.0.1` - **Source:** View on GitHub

chunks.title: File Streaming Job
chunks.heading: File Formats
chunks.text: - CSV - JSON - Amazon S3 with SQS notifications (`s3-sqs`), recommended for large or fast-growing buckets. See Amazon S3 with SQS.

chunks.title: File Streaming Job
chunks.heading: Marketplace

The Marketplace template opens a pre-filled **Create New Job** form. Review the source path and destination table in the config file (see Configuration) and update the values for your environment.

Name and Application** - **Name:** any name you like, for example `file-streaming-job` - **Application type:** `Python` - **Docker image:** `iomete.azurecr.io/iomete/iomete-file-streaming:1.0.1` (replace with the latest version) - **Main application file:** `local:///app/driver.py` **2. Environment Variables** - `LOG_LEVEL`: `INFO` or `ERROR` You can also use environment variables to store sensitive values, such as passwords or secrets, and reference them in your config file using the `$` syntax. **3. Spark Config** - `spark.sql.streaming.schemaInference`: `true` Set this when the config file doesn't provide an explicit `schema` for CSV. JSON and `s3-sqs` sources always need an explicit `schema` regardless of this setting. See Schema. **4. Config File** Expand **Configurations**, select the **Config Maps** tab, click **Add config**, and paste the HOCON template below. See Configuration for what each field does. { source: { file: { format: csv, header: true, path: "s3a://bucket/path_to_csv_files/", max_files_per_trigger: 1, latest_first: false, max_file_age: "7d" } } destination: processing_time: } **5. Instance Resources** Pick driver and executor instance types that fit your data volume. Click to save the job.

chunks.title: File Streaming Job
chunks.heading: Configuration
chunks.text: The config file is HOCON. It declares the source, the destination table, and the streaming trigger interval.

chunks.title: File Streaming Job
chunks.heading: Source File
chunks.text: format: Description File format to read: csv or json (still used when source.queue is set, to tell the job how to parse the notified files). See Amazon S3 with SQS.. header: Description Whether the CSV files include a header row (ignored when source.queue is set).. path: Description Source directory path, including the filesystem scheme, for example s3a://bucket/path_to_csv_files/ (ignored when source.queue is set).. max_files_per_trigger: Description Maximum number of new files to process per streaming trigger.. latest_first: Description Whether to process the latest files first when there is a backlog (ignored when source.queue is set).. max_file_age: Description Maximum age of files the stream considers, for example 7d.. filename_only: Description _Optional._ Detect new files by filename only instead of full path. Only enable this if filenames are unique across the entire source; otherwise files with the same name in different folders are treated as duplicates and skipped..

chunks.title: File Streaming Job
chunks.heading: Destination
chunks.text: schema: Description Destination schema (database).. table: Description Destination table.. partitions: Description _Optional._ Destination partition columns..

chunks.title: File Streaming Job
chunks.heading: Processing Time
chunks.text: interval: Description Streaming trigger interval.. unit: Description Trigger interval unit: seconds or minutes..

chunks.title: File Streaming Job
chunks.heading: Schema
chunks.text: CSV can infer its schema from the file (set `spark.sql.streaming.schemaInference: true` in Spark config) or use an explicit schema. JSON and `s3-sqs` sources always require an explicit schema; the job fails at startup with `Schema must be defined.` if one isn't provided. Add `schema` under `source` to define one explicitly: source: , { name: context, type: struct, properties: [ , ]} ]}, ] file: } Supported `type` values: - `string` - `int` (or `bigint`/`integer`) - `double` - `boolean` - `date` - `timestamp` (or `date-time`/`time`) - `array` (or `list`) - `struct`, for nested fields, with its own `properties`

chunks.title: File Streaming Job
chunks.heading: Amazon S3 with SQS
chunks.text: Listing a source directory on every trigger gets expensive as a bucket grows. If an SQS queue is subscribed to S3 object-created notifications for the bucket, point the job at the queue instead of the directory. Add `queue` under `source`. When `queue` is present, it takes over as the read path: the job still uses `source.file.format` to know how to parse the notified files, but `source.file.path`, `header`, and `latest_first` go unused. source: /" fetch_interval_seconds: 2 log_polling_wait_time_seconds: 5 } schema: [ ] file: } `source.file` is still required even when `queue` is set; the job reads it unconditionally at startup. Set `format` to match your files (`csv` or `json`); `path`, `header`, and `latest_first` are ignored in this mode but the keys must still be present. URL: Description SQS queue URL. The job parses the AWS region from this URL.. fetch_interval_seconds: Description How often to poll the queue for new file notifications.. log_polling_wait_time_seconds: Description Long-polling wait time for each SQS receive call.. `schema` is required when using the `s3-sqs` source. See Schema.

chunks.title: File Streaming Job
chunks.heading: Running the Job
chunks.text: Once deployed, the job runs continuously; there's no schedule to trigger. It reads new files as they arrive (or new SQS notifications, if configured) and appends them to the destination table on the configured `processing_time` interval.

chunks.heading: Configuration Properties

Set this to object storage for production, for example s3a://assets-dir/checkpoints/kafka-streaming/data/app1.. destination.database: Description Iceberg database name. The database must already exist.. destination.table: Description Iceberg table name. The job creates the table if it doesn't exist.. The job creates the destination table with the following schema: root |-- topic: string (nullable = true) |-- partition: integer (nullable = true) |-- offset: long (nullable = true) |-- timestamp: timestamp (nullable = true) |-- timestampType: integer (nullable = true) |-- key: string (nullable = true) |-- value: string (nullable = true) topic: Description The Kafka topic the record was received from.. partition: Description The Kafka partition the record was received from.. offset: Description The Kafka offset of the record.. timestamp: Description The Kafka timestamp of the record.. timestampType: Description The Kafka timestamp type of the record.. key: Description The Kafka record key.. value: Description The Kafka record value..

chunks.title: Kafka to Iceberg Streaming Job
chunks.heading: Configuration Properties
chunks.text: of the record.. key: Description The Kafka record key.. value: Description The Kafka record value..

chunks.title: Kafka to Iceberg Streaming Job
chunks.heading: Running the Job
chunks.text: With `trigger.once` set, the job processes everything currently available on the topic and stops. Trigger it again (or run it on a schedule) to pick up new records. With `trigger.processing_time` set, the job runs continuously, checking for new records at the given interval. To trigger a run on demand, open the job and click .

chunks.title: Lakehouse Backup Job
chunks.text: The **Lakehouse Backup Job** copies all files and folders under a configured storage path between S3-compatible object stores and HDFS-compatible storage. It preserves relative paths and runs file copies in parallel across a Spark cluster, so you can use the same job for scheduled backups and restores. - **Image:** `iomete.azurecr.io/iomete/iomete-lakehouse-backup: ` - **Latest version:** Marketplace Jobs release notes - **Source:** View on GitHub The job copies files as they exist during the run. It does not create a transactionally consistent snapshot while applications continue writing to the source. Run the backup when the source is not changing.

chunks.title: Lakehouse Backup Job
chunks.heading: Supported Storage Paths
chunks.text: You can configure either storage type as the source or target. S3: Target S3, Typical use Copy data to another bucket, account, region, or S3-compatible system.. S3: Target HDFS, Typical use Back up object-store data to Dell Isilon, OneFS, or Hadoop storage.. HDFS: Target S3, Typical use Restore or migrate HDFS data to object storage.. HDFS: Target HDFS, Typical use Copy data between HDFS-compatible systems.. S3 support includes AWS S3 and compatible systems such as Dell ECS and Ceph. HDFS support uses simple authentication and works with systems such as Dell Isilon, OneFS, and Hadoop clusters.

chunks.title: Lakehouse Backup Job
chunks.heading: Creating the Job Template
chunks.text: Before you create the job, make sure the source credentials allow reads and the target credentials allow writes. For HDFS, the Spark driver and executors must be able to reach the NameNode and every DataNode. 1. Open **Job Templates** and click **New Job Template**. See Creating a Spark Job for a walkthrough of the job form. 2. Configure the application: Docker image: Value iomete.azurecr.io/iomete/iomete-lakehouse-backup: . Main application file: Value spark-internal. Main class: Value com.iomete.backup.App. Arguments: Value /etc/configs/application.json. Replace ` ` with the version listed in the Marketplace Jobs release notes. 3. Choose an instance size for the amount of data you need to copy. 4. Under **Configurations → Config Maps**, add a file with the path `/etc/configs/application.json`, then paste your configuration. See Config Maps for details. 5. Add each credential as an environment variable whose name matches the `$` value in the JSON. Set its value from an IOMETE Secret (recommended). 6. Add a schedule if you want the backup to run automatically, then create the job. The selected instance normally supplies the executor count and CPU settings. If either value is missing, the run fails before copying data and reports the Spark setting you need to add: `spark.kubernetes.executor.limit.cores` and

chunks.title: Lakehouse Backup Job
chunks.heading: Creating the Job Template
chunks.text: normally supplies the executor count and CPU settings. If either value is missing, the run fails before copying data and reports the Spark setting you need to add: `spark.kubernetes.executor.limit.cores` and either `spark.executor.instances` or `spark.dynamicAllocation.maxExecutors`.

chunks.title: Lakehouse Backup Job
chunks.heading: Configuring an S3-to-S3 Backup
chunks.text: Use separate source and target credentials when the locations belong to different accounts or systems. { "source": { "type": "s3", "bucket": " ", "prefix": " ", "accessKey": "$", "secretKey": "$" }, "target": { "type": "s3", "bucket": " ", "prefix": " ", "accessKey": "$", "secretKey": "$" } } Replace the bucket and prefix placeholders with your storage locations. The job copies every source file under `SOURCE_PREFIX` to the same relative path under `TARGET_PREFIX`. For a non-AWS S3-compatible system, add its endpoint and enable path-style access when the system requires it: { "type": "s3", "bucket": "lakehouse-backup", "prefix": "production", "endpoint": "https://object-storage.example.com", "pathStyleAccess": true, "accessKey": "$", "secretKey": "$", "region": "us-east-1" }

chunks.title: Lakehouse Backup Job
chunks.heading: S3 Configuration
chunks.text: type: Required Yes, Default —, Description Set to s3.. bucket: Required Yes, Default —, Description S3 bucket name.. prefix: Required No, Default Empty, Description Folder prefix under the bucket.. endpoint: Required No, Default AWS default, Description Endpoint for an S3-compatible system.. pathStyleAccess: Required No, Default false, Description Uses path-style bucket addressing when set to true.. accessKey: Required Yes, Default —, Description Access key, normally provided through an IOMETE Secret.. secretKey: Required Yes, Default —, Description Secret key, normally provided through an IOMETE Secret.. region: Required No, Default us-east-1, Description S3 region..

chunks.title: Lakehouse Backup Job
chunks.heading: Configuring HDFS Storage
chunks.text: Use an HDFS block as either `source` or `target`. This example backs up S3 data to HDFS: { "source": { "type": "s3", "bucket": " ", "prefix": " ", "accessKey": "$", "secretKey": "$" }, "target": { "type": "hdfs", "namenode": "isilon.example.com:8020", "path": "backups/lakehouse", "user": "iomete-backup" } } For Dell Isilon or OneFS, use the SmartConnect zone FQDN for `namenode` so connections can be balanced across nodes. type: Required Yes, Default —, Description Set to hdfs.. namenode: Required Yes, Default —, Description NameNode RPC endpoint in host:port format.. path: Required No, Default Empty, Description Directory under the filesystem root.. user: Required Yes, Default —, Description HDFS user with the required read or write permissions.. authentication: Required No, Default simple, Description Authentication mode. Only simple is supported.. Simple authentication uses the configured user name without a password. Kerberos-secured HDFS clusters are not supported.

chunks.title: Lakehouse Backup Job
chunks.heading: Configuring Copy Behavior
chunks.text: The default copy settings work for most backups. Add a `copy` block when you need timestamped backup folders, a full copy, a bandwidth limit, or different performance settings. { "copy": { "skipIdentical": true, "targetTimestampFolder": "daily", "clockSkewToleranceMs": 30000, "slotsPerVcpu": 4, "tasksPerSlot": 20, "perFileOverheadBytes": 26214400, "maxBytesPerTask": 1073741824, "maxBandwidthMbPerSec": 600 } } skipIdentical: Default true, Description Skips a target file when its size matches and its modification time is sufficiently newer than the source. Set to false to copy every source file.. targetTimestampFolder: Default Unset, Description Adds an hourly, daily, weekly, or monthly UTC folder under the target path. Unset writes directly to the target path.. clockSkewToleranceMs: Default 30000, Description Required target timestamp margin when deciding whether a file is identical.. slotsPerVcpu: Default 4, Description Maximum concurrent file copies per executor vCPU.. tasksPerSlot: Default 20, Description Target number of Spark tasks per copy slot.. perFileOverheadBytes: Default 26214400, Description Estimated fixed per-file cost used to balance tasks. It does not add bytes to the copy.. maxBytesPerTask: Default 1073741824, Description Maximum estimated work assigned to a normal task. A larger individual file remains whole in its own task.. maxBandwidthMbPerSec: Default Unset, Description Maximum aggregate copy rate across the whole job in MB/s. Unset means uncapped..

chunks.title: Lakehouse Backup Job
chunks.heading: Configuring Copy Behavior
chunks.text: a normal task. A larger individual file remains whole in its own task.. maxBandwidthMbPerSec: Default Unset, Description Maximum aggregate copy rate across the whole job in MB/s. Unset means uncapped.. The job does not split individual files. It stages each write under a temporary target path, verifies that the written length matches the source, and then renames the file into place. It retries temporary failures and fails the run if any file cannot be copied. Files that exist only at the target are not deleted.

chunks.title: Lakehouse Backup Job
chunks.heading: Creating Timestamped Backup Folders
chunks.text: By default, every run copies files to the target path in your configuration. Changed files replace their existing copies, while files deleted from the source remain at the target. Set `targetTimestampFolder` when you want a separate target folder for each hour, day, week, or month. This example creates one folder per day: } If a run starts on February 14, 2026, the job appends `2026-02-14` to the configured target path. Folder names use the run start time in UTC: hourly: Folder example 2026-02-14-09. daily: Folder example 2026-02-14. weekly: Folder example 2026-W07. monthly: Folder example 2026-02. All runs that start in the same period use the same folder. For example, every `daily` run started on February 14 writes to `2026-02-14`. When `skipIdentical` is enabled, later runs skip files that are already present and unchanged, then copy only new or changed files. The job does not delete old timestamped folders or files that no longer exist at the source. Use a storage lifecycle rule or a separate cleanup job to remove them.

chunks.title: Lakehouse Backup Job
chunks.heading: Recording Run History
chunks.text: Run-history recording is enabled by default. The job creates these Iceberg tables on its first run: spark_catalog.iomete_system_db.lakehouse_backup_runs: Contents One row per run with status, counts, byte totals, stage timings, and copy settings.. spark_catalog.iomete_system_db.lakehouse_backup_run_file_failures: Contents One row per recorded file failure, joined by run_id.. To disable recording, change its database, or limit recorded failure rows, add a `stats` block: { "stats": { "enabled": true, "database": "spark_catalog.iomete_system_db", "maxFailureRows": 1000 } } enabled: Default true, Description Records run history when enabled.. database: Default spark_catalog.iomete_system_db, Description Database for both history tables. You can include or omit the catalog.. maxFailureRows: Default 1000, Description Maximum failure details stored for one run. The run table still records the full failure count.. A history-table write failure produces a warning but does not turn a successful backup into a failed run.

chunks.title: Lakehouse Backup Job
chunks.heading: Running and Checking a Backup
chunks.text: 1. Confirm that applications are not changing the source files. 2. Open the job template and start a run. 3. Monitor the run as described in Running a Spark Job. 4. After it finishes, query the run-history table: SELECT run_id, status, started_at, ended_at, files_copied, files_skipped, files_failed, bytes_copied, error_message FROM spark_catalog.iomete_system_db.lakehouse_backup_runs ORDER BY started_at DESC LIMIT 20; A complete backup has `status = 'SUCCEEDED'`, `files_failed = 0`, and a populated `ended_at`. A run that remains `RUNNING` long after it started usually means its driver stopped before recording the outcome. To inspect failed files, replace ` ` and run: SELECT source_path, target_path, attempts_used, error FROM spark_catalog.iomete_system_db.lakehouse_backup_run_file_failures WHERE run_id = ' ' ORDER BY source_path;

chunks.title: Lakehouse Backup Job
chunks.heading: Restoring a Backup
chunks.text: Create a separate job template for restores so a scheduled backup cannot accidentally run with reversed locations. Configure the backup location as `source` and the restore location as `target`, then run it while the restore target is not being written by another process. For example, restore an HDFS backup to S3 with: { "source": { "type": "hdfs", "namenode": "isilon.example.com:8020", "path": "backups/lakehouse", "user": "iomete-backup" }, "target": { "type": "s3", "bucket": " ", "prefix": " ", "accessKey": "$", "secretKey": "$" } } After the run succeeds, validate the restored catalog or workload against the copied files before directing production traffic to it.

chunks.title: Lakehouse Backup Job
chunks.heading: Tuning Copy Performance
chunks.text: Start with the defaults and compare successful runs of the same source before changing anything. The run-history table separates source listing, target listing, planning, copy, and directory-creation time, and it records effective concurrency and task shape. - Raise `slotsPerVcpu` only when copy slots stay busy and additional concurrency continues to improve throughput. - Raise `tasksPerSlot` when too few tasks leave slots idle near the end of the copy. - Raise `perFileOverheadBytes` when tasks containing many small files run much longer than others. - Set `maxBandwidthMbPerSec` when the backup must leave network capacity for other workloads. For the full metrics reference and tuning queries, see Backup run history. To benchmark controlled configuration changes in your environment, follow the load-testing runbook.

chunks.title: MySQL Database Replication Job
chunks.text: --- The **MySQL Database Replication Job** copies tables from a MySQL database into the IOMETE Lakehouse on a schedule. You point the job at a source database, list the tables to sync, choose between a full reload or an incremental snapshot, and the job handles the rest. - **Version:** see the Marketplace Jobs release notes for the latest version - **Source:** View on GitHub

chunks.title: MySQL Database Replication Job
chunks.heading: Marketplace
chunks.text: Open **Job Templates** and click **Marketplace**. Find the **mysql-sync** card, click the **⋮** menu, and select **Deploy**. The job form opens pre-filled with recommended defaults. Add your database password as an environment variable and your sync rules as a config file (see Configuration), then click **Create**. To customize the template, copy it from the Marketplace into your own job and adjust as needed.

chunks.title: MySQL Database Replication Job
chunks.heading: Manual Setup
chunks.text: Open **Job Templates** in the sidebar and click . **1. Name and Application** - **Name:** any name you like, for example `mysql-db-sync` - **Application type:** `Python` - **Docker image:** `iomete.azurecr.io/iomete/iomete_mysql_sync: ` (see Marketplace Jobs release notes for the latest version) - **Main application file:** `local:///app/driver.py` **2. Environment Variables** Store the database password as an environment variable rather than checking it into the config file. Add a variable named `DB_PASSWORD` with your MySQL password as the value, then reference it from the config as `$`. **3. Config File** Expand **Application configurations**, click **Add config file**, and paste the HOCON template below. See Configuration for what each field does. { source_connection: { host: "your-mysql-host.example.com", port: 3306, username: mysql_user, password: $\ }, syncs: [ { source.schema: employees source.tables: ["*"] source.exclude_tables: [departments, dept_manager] destination.schema: employees_raw sync_mode.type: full_load } ] } **4. Instance Resources** Pick driver and executor instance types that fit your data volume. Click to save the job.

chunks.title: MySQL Database Replication Job
chunks.heading: Configuration
chunks.text: The config file is HOCON. It declares the source MySQL connection and one or more sync entries.

chunks.title: MySQL Database Replication Job
chunks.heading: Source Connection
chunks.text: host: Description The address of the MySQL database, for example your-mysql-host.example.com.. port: Description The MySQL port, usually 3306.. username: Description The MySQL user the job connects as.. password: Description The user's password. Reference an environment variable like $ rather than embedding the value..

chunks.title: MySQL Database Replication Job
chunks.heading: Syncs
chunks.text: The `syncs` array contains one or more sync entries. Each entry describes a source schema, the tables to include, the destination schema in IOMETE, and the sync mode. source.schema: Description The schema in the MySQL database to read from.. source.tables: Description The tables to sync. Use [""] to include every table in the schema. You can also pass a SQL subquery as a virtual table — see Subquery Sources.. source.exclude_tables: Description _Optional._ Tables to skip when source.tables is [""].. destination.schema: Description The schema in the IOMETE Lakehouse where rows are written.. sync_mode.type: Description Either full_load or incremental_snapshot. See Sync Modes..

chunks.title: MySQL Database Replication Job
chunks.heading: `full_load`
chunks.text: Reads everything from the source table and overwrites the destination table on every run. Use this for small or slowly-changing tables where you want each run to be a clean snapshot.

chunks.title: MySQL Database Replication Job
chunks.heading: `incremental_snapshot`
chunks.text: Brings over only rows inserted or updated since the last run, using a `MERGE` statement against a snapshot of the table in the destination. Use this for large tables where a full reload is too expensive. This mode requires two extra fields: sync_mode.identification_column: Description The primary key column used in the merge condition, typically id.. sync_mode.tracking_column: Description A monotonically increasing column the job uses to find new rows since the last sync, typically updated_at. The column must be set on every insert and update..

chunks.title: MySQL Database Replication Job
chunks.heading: Subquery Sources
chunks.text: Instead of a table name, an entry in `source.tables` can be a SQL subquery wrapped in triple-quoted HOCON strings, with an alias. This replicates a derived view rather than a raw table. source.tables: [ """ (SELECT emp_no, sum(salary) total_salary FROM salaries group by emp_no) as total_salaries """ ] The job replicates the subquery result into a destination table named after the alias (`total_salaries` in this example).

chunks.title: MySQL Database Replication Job
chunks.heading: Example 1: Full Load Excluding Some Tables
chunks.text: Replicates every table in the `employees` schema except `salaries` into `employees_raw` on each run. { source.schema: employees source.tables: ["*"] source.exclude_tables: [salaries] destination.schema: employees_raw sync_mode.type: full_load }

chunks.title: MySQL Database Replication Job
chunks.heading: Example 2: Specific Tables Full Load
chunks.text: Replicates only the `departments` and `dept_manager` tables. { source.schema: employees source.tables: [departments, dept_manager] destination.schema: employees_raw sync_mode.type: full_load }

chunks.title: MySQL Database Replication Job
chunks.heading: Example 3: Incremental Snapshot
chunks.text: Brings over only new or changed rows in the `salaries` table, using `id` as the primary key and `updated_at` as the change-tracking column. { source.schema: employees source.tables: [salaries] destination.schema: employees_raw sync_mode: { type: incremental_snapshot identification_column: id tracking_column: updated_at } }

chunks.title: MySQL Database Replication Job
chunks.heading: Running the Job
chunks.text: The job runs on its schedule. To trigger a run on demand, open the job and click . To change the schedule, edit the job and set the **Schedule** parameter (cron expression).

chunks.title: Query Scheduler Job
chunks.text: --- **IOMETE** provides **Query Scheduler Job** to run your warehouse queries on a schedule or manually.

chunks.title: Query Scheduler Job

chunks.text: - In the left sidebar, under **Applications**, click **Job Templates**. - Click to open the list of preconfigured Marketplace jobs. - Find `query-scheduler-job`, open the actions menu, and click . - The Marketplace template opens a pre-filled **Create New Job** form. Review the defaults and update the values for your environment. You can also create a job template manually with **New Job Template**, but the Marketplace flow is recommended because it pre-populates the Query Scheduler image, schedule, environment variables, and default query configuration. Specify the following parameters (these are examples, you can change them based on your preference): - **Name:** `query-scheduler-job` - **Schedule:** `0 0/22 1/1 * *` - **Docker image:** `iomete/spark-py:3.5.7-v1` - **Main application file:** `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/iomete/query-scheduler-job/main/job.py` - **Environment variables:** `LOG_LEVEL`: `INFO`

chunks.text: - **Config file:** The Marketplace template includes a default query configuration under the `Config Maps` tab. Review the queries and update them for your environment.

chunks.title: Query Scheduler Job
chunks.heading: Queries to be run sequentially
chunks.text: [ # let's create an example SELECT """ SELECT 1 """ ] Click **Create** after reviewing the job configuration.
